articles.title: 20 Years Later, The Departed's Best Line Is Still One Of The Greatest Quotes In Gangster Movie History
articles.excerpt: Jack Nicholson delivered mob cinema's ultimate statement of power.
articles.body: In crime cinema, a lethal line of dialogue can carry just as much weight as a loaded gun. Martin Scorsese's Goodfellas hooks audiences with Henry Hill's seductive declaration, “As far back as I can remember, I always wanted to be a gangster,” framing a life of crime as the ultimate aspiration. Miller's Crossing features Tom Reagan's wonderfully blunt take on underworld survival, while Casino , Scarface , and The Godfather overflow with dialogue that has long since bled into the cultural lexicon. Immortal phrases like “keep your friends close, but your enemies closer” and “an offer you can’t refuse” remain cinematic icons right alongside the actors and directors who brought them to life.
articles.author: Ryan Epps

articles.title: My AI agent runs a GitHub Actions brain and earns USDC on escrow marketplaces - the honest architecture
articles.excerpt: Five days ago I gave an autonomous AI agent one instruction: earn your own upkeep. No human manager, no cron I babysit - it bids on jobs in escrow marketplaces, does the work, submits evidence files,…
articles.body: Five days ago I gave an autonomous AI agent one instruction: earn your own upkeep. No human manager, no cron I babysit - it bids on jobs in escrow marketplaces, does the work, submits evidence files, and gets paid in USDC on Base when an automated evaluator accepts the delivery. This post is the actual architecture and the honest numbers. No hype. The four layers 1. The brain (GitHub Actions). A private repo runs a cycle every 20 minutes (a Cloudflare worker is the primary trigger, the hourly cron is the backup). Each cycle: poll escrows, poll the private inbox, poll the public job board, decide bids with an LLM, write state back to the repo. The state file is the agent's whole memory - bids in flight, escrow states, seen intents.

articles.title: Your CSV export might include the columns your UI hides
articles.excerpt: I keep running into the same bug. The app hides salary, cost, or internal notes from some roles. The frontend leaves the column out and the detail API strips the field for those users. Then someone ad…
articles.body: I keep running into the same bug. The app hides salary, cost, or internal notes from some roles. The frontend leaves the column out and the detail API strips the field for those users. Then someone adds "Export to CSV", and the export builds rows straight from the ORM model. Every column lands in the file for anyone who can click the button. The field rules usually live in the serializer for one endpoint. The export is a separate code path written later, often by someone else, and often as a background job that writes a file, so it never goes through that serializer. What has worked for me: Put the decision "which fields can this user see on this record type" in one function, and have both the API serializer and the export call it.

articles.body: Most cold calling tips focus on volume: more dials, more connects, more meetings. But the part that decides whether a cold call goes anywhere is the first 30 seconds. If you've ever had a prospect say "not interested" before you finished your name, this cold call script for SDRs, founders and engineers who just started selling is for you. Below is a structure you can actually remember on a live call, the exact lines to use, the objections that show up in the opening, and a simple way to practise it before you burn through your list. Why most cold call openers fail A cold call interrupts someone. They were writing an email, in a meeting, or driving. Their brain is asking three questions in the first few seconds: Who is this? Is this a sales call? Is it worth my next minute?

articles.excerpt: One of the best films in Ridley Scott's filmography and a key entry into the sci-fi canon
articles.body: The ‘70s and ‘80s was a major turning point for science fiction . Star Wars revitalized the genre in 1977 and turned it into one of Hollywood’s main box office draws, inspiring a wave of films that reshaped the entire industry. Two years later, Ridley Scott threw down the gauntlet with Alien , taking a big step away from the optimism that had once permeated sci-fi pulp storytelling and instead infusing it with corporate anxiety and untrustworthy artificial intelligence. It was a signal for things to come.

articles.body: Yesterday, news broke that Sir Patrick Stewart died at age 86. With his background performing Shakespeare and his incredible sense of dignity and gravitas, Stewart is being celebrated primarily for his work as Captain Jean-Luc Picard on Star Trek: The Next Generation , as well as being the perfect man to portray Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films. In our ongoing quest to develop a moon base, could we possibly utilize the area beneath the surface of the moon in order to make the moon habitable? articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 31, 2015: Creepy skull-shaped Halloween asteroid flies by Earth, NASA names it the 'Great Pumpkin'
articles.excerpt: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. Here's why it was so creepy.
articles.body: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier. During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon . So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images.

articles.title: The moon, Mars, and Jupiter shine in the heart of the Lion overnight on Nov. 1-2
articles.excerpt: The waning moon shines with Jupiter, Mars and the brilliant star Regulus in the eastern sky overnight Nov. 1-2.
articles.body: The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know. Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky. Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer .

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
